clue.text: The skinhead tried to change step

indicators.note: the letters of tried are made to change their order into a new arrangement

blocks.note: read as skin's head: the opening letter of skin
the five letters of tried, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A skinhead attempts to alter the way he walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like one word for a shaven youth, but it splits into skin plus head, the first letter of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long walking pace, so it is a synonym of step as a noun.

clue.text: Small traveller who's prepared for takeoff

definitions.note: a noun phrase: one who is prepared

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a tripper is someone on a day trip or outing

explanation.surface: A little passenger waits for the plane to leave the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takeoff' suggests an aircraft departing; read as take off, it means removing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer whose act consists of removing clothing is ready to take garments off, hence a punning description.

clue.text: Checks taxes - not for the first time!

blocks.note: RE- is the prefix meaning again, so something done not for the first time
to tax something is to put it under strain, as in strains

explanation.surface: An exasperated taxpayer complains about yet another tax demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxes' reads as a noun for levies but is a verb meaning puts a burden on.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or curb, so restrains is a synonym of checks used as a verb.

clue.text: There's very little to deposit

blocks.note: first meaning: a tiny amount, as in just a small quantity of liquid
second meaning: to set down or let fall, as in leaving a parcel somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone notes there is hardly anything worth putting in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a tiny quantity of liquid and a verb for setting something down or delivering it.

clue.text: Pole taking are returned shabby case

indicators.note: the pole is followed by what it takes, so the pieces are joined one after another
something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: S stands for the South Pole
the scan shows are, but the printed word must be cab, a taxi, taken as written
drab means dull and dowdy, a synonym of shabby

explanation.surface: A Polish passenger hails a taxi, carrying a worn-out suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper scan misreads cab as are; with cab restored, 'Pole' is the S of a compass pole, not a person from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword, a kind of protective case for a blade.

clue.text: Sticking together or parting?

blocks.note: first meaning: clinging or adhering closely
second meaning: splitting apart, as with an axe through wood

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark points to a contronym, a word carrying two opposite senses: to cleave can mean to cling or to split.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb cleave has two unrelated origins, one meaning adhere closely and one meaning split apart with force.

clue.text: Fought foreign currency racket

blocks.note: to battle is to fight
the öre is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone struggled against a scam involving overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests a swindle, but here it is a bat for hitting a shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is the small wooden or strung bat used in the old game of battledore and shuttlecock, the ancestor of badminton.

clue.text: Jotter Pad 7 Bring a well qualified person in with all speed

blocks.note: not part of the clue: page debris picked up from the scanned newspaper
taken as written
an MA is a Master of Arts, a holder of a higher degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fetch an expert into the room as quickly as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jotter Pad 7' is page debris from the scanned newspaper and is not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Amain is an archaic adverb meaning at full speed or with full force, matching the phrase given.

clue.text: "Men love in haste, but they - at leisure" (Byron)

definitions.text: "Men love in haste, but they - at leisure" (Byron)

blocks.clueFragment: "Men love in haste, but they - at leisure"
blocks.note: surface reading: a famous line about fickle men with a word missing
setter's reading: supply the missing verb from Byron's Don Juan, the opposite of love

explanation.walkthrough: Byron's line echoes the proverb 'marry in haste, repent at leisure'; the gap wants the verb that contrasts with love.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes the poet's quotation, contrasting quick affection with slow, lasting hatred.

clue.text: Study is to be made of renal failure

indicators.note: a failure is a breakdown, so the letters of the word before it fall apart and regroup

blocks.note: the letters of renal, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical student is told to research kidney disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renal failure' reads as a medical condition, but failure is the signal and renal is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to acquire knowledge, and study is a verb with that same meaning.

clue.text: Having to do with the shop making refund

blocks.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: A customer at a shop is getting money back.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore is to give back what was taken, so it works as a verb synonym of refund.

clue.text: Draw for use of spare court

blocks.note: an extra is a spare, something additional
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A tennis club holds a ballot for who gets the unused court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests a raffle or a tied match; here it is the verb meaning pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull something out, as you draw a tooth or draw water from a well.

clue.text: Coppers are so trim

blocks.note: coppers are pennies, and p is the abbreviation for pence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police officers are fit and slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police officers; in Britain it is also slang for low-value bronze coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to cut away the outer edge or skin, so it is a verb synonym of trim.

clue.text: Threatening the railways on the Channel coast

definitions.note: the clue describes where the town is rather than naming it

blocks.note: a grave situation is serious and menacing
railway lines, the routes trains run on

explanation.surface: A rail network near the sea is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravelines is a French port town between Calais and Dunkirk.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Gravelines lies in northern France beside the strait between England and France, so it sits on that coast.

clue.text: In a sense the German appears devious

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the German article goes inside the sense

blocks.note: meaning is a synonym of sense, as in the sense of a word
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German man seems underhand in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German' suggests a person, but it is the German definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Devious can mean winding or roundabout, as well as sly, and a twisting path is one that wanders about.

clue.text: Formerly one was the first to be banished

blocks.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
I is the Roman numeral one
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A former leader became the first to be sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiled describes someone expelled from their own country, a direct synonym of banished as a past participle.

clue.text: Awfully annoyed - comforting's called for!

indicators.note: doing something awfully means doing it badly, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of annoyed, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is very cross, and consolation is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means soothing or pain-relieving, and an anodyne was originally a painkiller that eased distress.

clue.text: Being terribly scathing about quiet wear for retired people

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the word after it is scrambled
about means around, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: the letters of scathing, rearranged
p stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone is harshly critical about a hushed matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired people' suggests pensioners; here it means people who have gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightcaps are soft hats once worn in bed, so they are clothing for those who have turned in for the night.

clue.text: Indoor interest

blocks.note: first meaning: read as in-door, the doorway by which you go in
second meaning: as a verb with stress on the second syllable, to charm or captivate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Indoor interest' sounds like a hobby; split it into a way in and a verb for enchanting.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a doorway giving access, and the verb, stressed differently, means to fill with delight or wonder.

clue.text: Opinion held about employees in residence

indicators.note: a belief held about others wraps around them, so the opinion encloses the next piece

blocks.note: a tenet is a belief or principle
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A view is held about the staff living on site.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building of rented flats, a place of dwelling, so it fits residence as a noun.

clue.text: A fall from grace in the orient would be stupid

blocks.note: taken as written
a sin is a moral lapse
taken as written
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A moral lapse while travelling in Asia would be foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine literally means like an ass, so it is a synonym for foolish or silly.

clue.text: Minor villain going on foot

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something that goes on the foot

blocks.note: B denotes second-rate, as in a B-movie
a rogue is a rascal or crook

explanation.surface: A petty crook makes his escape on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going on foot' sounds like walking, but it describes a shoe, which goes on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations, an item worn over the foot.

clue.text: A girl may take these letters, having the right

indicators.note: a name that may take a set of letters can use them in any order it likes

blocks.note: the clue points to the letters of the word these themselves
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A girl writing her name needs these letters plus one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a female first name, so it is an example of what a girl may be called.

clue.text: Present that's simply not on with royalty

blocks.note: off is the opposite of on
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A gift that simply isn't appropriate for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a noun for a gift but is the verb meaning put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer something is to hold it out for acceptance, a synonym of the verb present.

clue.text: The Penzance Pirates' ship?

blocks.note: surface reading: the vessel sailed by the buccaneers in Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta
setter's reading: a theatre company's boat is only a prop, a vessel that floats on the boards; read it as a word for theatrical skill

explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; any pirate ship in it is a piece of scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means skill in theatrical production, but split in two it describes a vessel built for the theatre.

clue.text: Rider in the main backing recesses

indicators.note: one item placed in another goes inside it
backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: the main is a poetic term for the open ocean
a rider is an addition to a document, like a PS or postscript

explanation.surface: A horseman at sea reverses into some alcoves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horseman; it is an added clause, a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Apses are the semicircular recesses at the end of a church, so they are architectural recesses.

clue.text: This may well cause the viewer much irritation

definitions.text: This may well cause the viewer much irritation

blocks.clueFragment: This may well cause the viewer much irritation
blocks.note: surface reading: a dreadful television programme that annoys its audience
setter's reading: the viewer is the eye, and the answer is an inflamed swelling on its lid

explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small painful infection at the edge of the eyelid, which irritates the organ we see with.

clue.text: Facts an American lawyer put to certain soldiers

blocks.note: a DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A US attorney presents evidence to a group of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are pieces of information gathered for analysis, a synonym of facts in the plural.

clue.text: She's perverse and in a mess - that's material

indicators.note: something perverse goes against the normal way, so the word before it is jumbled
a mess is a muddle, so the two short words in front of it are jumbled as well

blocks.note: the letters of she's without the apostrophe
the letters of in a

explanation.surface: A contrary woman is in a muddle, and that's what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like an adjective meaning important; it is a noun for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse fabric woven from jute or hemp, so it is a kind of material or cloth.

clue.text: Come out in support of the man at executive level

indicators.note: the words that follow hold up the answer, which sits inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these four words

explanation.surface: Employees declare their backing for the boss at board level.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or issue from a source, which matches come out.

clue.text: Gave up being passive

blocks.note: first meaning: quit a job or post
second meaning: accepting something unpleasant without protest

explanation.surface: Someone quit because they had become apathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of quitting a post and an adjective for calmly accepting what cannot be changed.

clue.text: The hound lay full of dope

indicators.note: something full of a thing has it inside, so the wager encloses the fool

blocks.note: a lay is a wager, as in to lay money on a horse
a dope is a fool, as is an ass

explanation.surface: The dog was lying down, drugged up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' and 'dope' suggest a sleeping, drugged dog, but they are a wager and a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged breed of scent hound with long ears, so it is an example of a hound.
